quotes.text:
* PRTime --
 *
 *     NSPR represents basic time as 64-bit signed integers relative
 *     to midnight (00:00:00), January 1, 1970 Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).
 *     (GMT is also known as Coordinated Universal Time, UTC.)
 *     The units of time are in microseconds. Negative times are allowed
 *     to represent times prior to the January 1970 epoch. Such values are
 *     intended to be exported to other systems or converted to human
 *     readable form.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: 841 adds maildir file modification time as envelope time. The fixed accepted scanner passes GetLastModifiedTime output directly to onStartMessage; StoreIndexer passes it unchanged to the parser. Gecko nsIFile documents milliseconds, while NSPR PRTime documents microseconds. The parser seeds its date from that value and later calls SetDate; a successfully parsed Date header replaces the envelope value. Thus the concern applies to the envelope fallback path. This is an unresolved static unit mismatch, despite matching C++ types. No repair was reproduced, no fix was made, and the inspected dateless test does not explicitly select both store types. The inspected Gecko documentation is at a separately recorded accepted revision; exact comm-to-Gecko revision pairing was not verified.
title: Check timestamp units even when both APIs use PRTime
